title: Revealing Medium Range Ordering in Zr-based Metallic Glasses Using Machine Learning Analysis of 4D-STEM Nanodiffraction
content: Nanoscale electron beams, such as those used in 4D-STEM, enable the local structural analysis of disordered materials, revealing nanoscale structural heterogeneity and the constituent medium-range ordering (MRO) that influences their properties. This spatially resolved structural information complements the global, averaged structure obtained from large-area diffraction techniques, such as the pair distribution function. While nanodiffraction has been employed to study amorphous and glassy materials, ongoing efforts continue to address the challenges of reliably extracting MRO information. In this work, we present a new machine learning (ML) analysis of 4D-STEM data from Zr-based metallic glasses (MGs), revealing the classification of MRO structures with unprecedented details. We demonstrate that the distinct types and distributions of MRO vary with MG composition, directly impacting their properties. This provides new insights into how the nanoscale structure of disordered materials can be controlled to optimize properties, such as achieving both high yield strength and ductility simultaneously in MGs.
